video_title: Scottie Barnes | Post Game vs New York Knicks | November 15, 2026

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on the origin of his hip injury
quotes.excerpt: I think the hip was hurting. I think we already seen the hit was hurting.
quotes.quote: I think the hip was hurting. I think we already seen the hit was hurting. And then I think the groin came, maybe Denver game, and then it was just rough for me sleeping that night, laying down, just relaxing by myself, so it became more serious.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes reveals his hip and groin injuries became more serious after the Denver game, noting it was rough for him even just trying to sleep at night.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes explains the timeline and severity of his hip and groin injuries during a post-game media availability.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on late-game mistakes against the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Got a five-second call. Those are two terrible mistakes that we just got to have.
quotes.quote: For sure we got to come over there with a big-time rebound. Got a five-second call. Those are two terrible mistakes that we just got to have in that game. Give ourselves the best chance to win that game and that was pretty tough.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes points to a missed rebound and a five second call as the two terrible mistakes that cost the Raptors the game against the Knicks.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes reflects on late-game errors including a missed rebound and a five-second violation against the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on the championship resilience of the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: They won championship last year and that's what championship teams do, they stay resilient.
quotes.quote: They won championship last year and that's what championship teams do, they stay resilient, they stay through those moments and that's what they did. They got big threes, they start running offense, they just figured out a way to come back into that game and win.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes on the Knicks resilience: They won a championship last year and that is what championship teams do. They stay through those moments and they figured out a way to win.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes discusses the resilience displayed by the New York Knicks during their comeback victory.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on the need to stop playing to secure wins
quotes.excerpt: We just got to stop trying to kind of plan to secure the win.
quotes.quote: We just got to stop trying to kind of plan to secure the win. Keep playing fast, keep running random actions, keep getting some ball movement. We're coming down, playing a half court, trying to call a play, but as players we just got to get the ball and just run.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes says the Raptors need to stop playing to secure the win and instead keep playing fast and running random actions to close out games.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes discusses the need for the Raptors to maintain pace and ball movement rather than slowing down to protect a lead.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on the defensive impact of OG Anunoby and Miles McBride
quotes.excerpt: OG's physical, off-ball, great on-ball, and then McBride really in that fourth quarter, he got four or five stops.
quotes.quote: OG's physical, off-ball, great on-ball, and then McBride really in that fourth quarter, he got four or five stops, probably like two steals. He was just being super aggressive, being super physical, which kind of really changed the game for them, I feel like, and letting them come back into the game.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes credits Miles McBride for changing the game in the fourth quarter, noting his super aggressive and physical defense helped the Knicks come back.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes credits the defensive aggression of OG Anunoby and Miles McBride for changing the game in the fourth quarter.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on the difficulty of guarding Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: His footwork when he's getting downhill, being able to create different angles and attack those angles.
quotes.quote: Obviously a really great player. His footwork when he's getting downhill, being able to create different angles and attack those angles, obviously makes him so good. He gets the two, he got the turnaround, he got the step through. And then when you play him in pick and coverage, try to guard him on the perimeter, obviously they have Karl-Anthony Towns, which is a great three-point shooter, so you still got to worry about those two as well.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes breaks down the difficulty of guarding Jalen Brunson, citing his footwork and ability to create angles while also having to account for Karl Anthony Towns.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes breaks down the difficulty of defending Jalen Brunson and the spacing provided by Karl-Anthony Towns.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on late-game execution and turnovers
quotes.excerpt: It just comes down to late game execution. We got to stop teams when they're going on runs.
quotes.quote: It just comes down to late game execution. We got to stop teams when they're going on runs. We just got to keep focus on our game plan and we got to execute at a high level. They got some offensive rebounds, obviously we got some late game mistakes, rebounds and turnovers, but that's what separates teams right there.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes says late game execution, specifically rebounding and turnovers, is what separates teams after the Raptors loss to New York.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes identifies late-game execution, rebounding, and turnovers as the factors that decided the game.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on the Knicks' late-game offensive execution
quotes.excerpt: They ran some action with Karl-Anthony Towns trailing the play and then people setting back screens.
quotes.quote: They ran some action with Karl-Anthony Towns trailing the play and then people setting back screens and they were coming over the top, getting to the paint easy, getting free shots. We did a great job throughout the game, but at the end of the game they were just getting those.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes explains that the Knicks late game offense relied on Karl Anthony Towns trailing plays and back screens to get easy shots in the paint.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes explains how the Knicks utilized Karl-Anthony Towns in late-game offensive sets to get easy shots.

quotes.speaker: Scottie Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Scottie Barnes on the value of watching film after a tough loss
quotes.excerpt: We lost a game that we know we could have won for sure.
quotes.quote: We lost a game that we know we could have won for sure. That it was going back and forth, but I think as we all watch the film, you know, this one's really going to sting and that's what's going to have to create those uncomfortable conversations when we get to practice tomorrow.
quotes.social_post: Scottie Barnes expects some uncomfortable conversations at practice tomorrow after the Raptors loss to the Knicks, saying this one is really going to sting.

structured.context: Scottie Barnes discusses the importance of reviewing game film and having difficult conversations after a tough loss.
